item.title: Local house prices continue to rise
item.description: House prices in the Shannonside region have seen a strong surge in the last 12 months. That's according to the latest national survey from the Real Estate Alliance which looks at the average second-hand three-bed semi. County Leitrim's prices rose to €225,000, up 13.9 per cent. Advertisement A 13.3 per cent increase is reported in county Longford with prices now standing at €221,000 While county Roscommon's have increased by 6.9 per cent to €270,000. item.title: Hospitals continue to deal with overcrowding
item.description: Local hospitals are continuing to deal with overcrowding. According to the INMO's latest trolley watch report, there were 44 waiting at Sligo University Hospital this morning. This included 25 in the emergency department and 19 on wards elsewhere. Advertisement Meanwhile, there were 22 patients waiting at Portiuncula Hospital and 1 in the Midland Regional Hospital in Mullingar.

item.title: Protest over Dunmore traffic congestion to take place
item.description: Part of a national road connecting east Mayo, Sligo and Roscommon with Galway is not fit for purpose, according to a protest group. Locals in Dunmore, County Galway say the section of the N83 through their town is dangerously narrow. They're calling for derelict buildings on either side of the road to be demolished so it can be widened, and vehicles don't have to mount footpaths to get by. item.title: Three hospitalised following Longford crashes
item.description: Three people have been hospitalised following two separate crashes in county Longford. The first collision took place in the Feraghfad area shortly after 8am on Sunday morning. The driver of the car, a man in his 30s was brought to the Midlands Regional Hospital in Tullamore for treatment of serious injuries. item.title: Fight continues for new Carrick school building
item.description: Frustration remains in Carrick-on-Shannon over the lack of a new school building for the town. It's almost ten years since the application was made for a new build for Scoil Mhuire. Pupil numbers have almost doubled in that time, to around 500, with the school located over two campuses, and some classes held in prefabs and subdivided rooms. item.title: Local schools sanctioned special education classes
item.description: A number of schools in the Shannonside region have been sanctioned for special education classes. The classes were announced by the Minister of Education and Youth, Hildegarde Naughton today. Both Cloonakilla National School and Roxboro National School will receive two new classes each. item.title: Hopes Mercosur deal can still be stopped
item.description: One of the organisers of Saturday's major Mercosur protest in Athlone says the deal can still be stopped. MEP Ciaran Mullooly was speaking after a petition signed by more than 30 thousand people opposing the deal was delivered in Brussels today. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyden plans to travel to South America this month to sign the agreement.
